root_causes.description: The checkout service exhibits a flat p99 latency of exactly 10000ms while every downstream dependency it calls (cart, payment, email, shipping, product-catalog) remains healthy at 2-49ms. With zero errors, normal CPU (0.005 cores) and memory (~25MB), and no pod events, the latency is intrinsic to checkout itself — consistent with an injected ~10s processing delay in the checkout request/order-consumed path.

evidence.observed_value: memory_usage=24923648 bytes (~25MB, max 25731072) — no memory stress
evidence.expected_baseline: memory_usage well below limits — rules out memory_stress

evidence.query_or_id: search_traces service_name=checkout min_duration_ms=5000: 1bca1a849d24103a (order-consumed, 25976ms, ok), 7d400ab9ff936ed0 (order-consumed, 9050ms, ok), c0107f4466e54abb (order-consumed, 10243ms, ok)
evidence.observed_value: 20 traces >5s, 0 with errors, p95_duration=661203ms; slow traces complete successfully
evidence.expected_baseline: checkout traces typically complete in <100ms with ok status

evidence.observed_value: [no K8s events found] — no OOMKilled/BackOff/crash events
evidence.expected_baseline: no restart events — rules out pod_crash

root_causes.description: Frontend p99 latency spiked to 10000ms, matching checkout exactly, because checkout is a synchronous dependency in the frontend request path. Frontend's other dependencies (cart, ad, currency, recommendation, product-catalog, shipping) show no anomalies, so the frontend latency is propagated impact from the faulted checkout service rather than a frontend-local fault.

Secondary hypothesis: the delay is localized in checkout's Kafka order-consumed processing path rather than the synchronous gRPC request handlers — all slow traces observed are 'order-consumed' spans (9050-25976ms) that eventually succeed, suggesting a per-message processing delay (e.g., injected sleep or blocking I/O in the order consumer loop).

evidence.observed_value: All top slow traces are span name 'order-consumed' with status ok, durations 9050ms/10243ms/25976ms

remediation_steps: Check the checkout deployment for an active chaos/latency fault injection (e.g., flagd feature flag, LATENCY/DELAY env var, or injected sleep in request handlers) and disable the ~10s artificial delay.
Inspect checkout application code and configuration for blocking calls, lock contention, or synchronous waits in the order-consumed Kafka consumer loop that add ~10s per operation.
Add a client-side timeout and circuit breaker on frontend→checkout calls (e.g., 2-3s budget) so a slow checkout cannot stall the entire user-facing request path at 10s.
After removing the delay, verify checkout p99 returns to baseline (<100ms) and confirm frontend p99 recovers, then close the incident.
Add a latency SLO alert on checkout p99 (>1s for 2m) to catch future injected or regressive delays faster.
